The server-side auth probe doesn't "see" a browser session directly — it never has access to the browser's own cookie jar during SSR. The chain in the graph: `auth.guards.ts` ([170], FE auth & interceptors) injects `session-state.service.ts` (14 ext in-edges, the auth-state hub), which calls `user.service.ts` and ultimately the collapsed generated OpenAPI client (`api`, in [177]) to ask the backend who the current user is. That outgoing HTTP call passes through the interceptor chain registered in `app.config.ts` ([177], the SSR/browser bootstrap config), which INJECTS `ssr-cookie-forward.interceptor.ts` ([170], `core/interceptors/`). This interceptor is the mechanism that gives the server-side probe a "session" at all: since Angular Universal's server-side `HttpClient` runs in Node with no browser cookie storage, this interceptor forwards the cookies from the original incoming request (the one the browser sent to the Node/SSR server) onto the outgoing API call, so the backend sees the same session cookie it would have seen from the browser directly.

Open `ssr-cookie-forward.interceptor.ts` (frontend `src/app/core/interceptors/ssr-cookie-forward.interceptor.ts`) for the exact header-copy logic, and `app.config.ts` to confirm it's wired only for the server platform. The precise cookie names/headers forwarded are file content, not graph-visible.

Invoice creation in this codebase is decoupled from payment success via the domain-event pattern: subsystem [11] (Subscriptions, payments & consent) emits `InvoiceCreatedEvent.java` (Event, [11]), which affects `InvoiceRecord.java` (the invoice entity/status record) and is picked up by `InvoiceCreatedEventListener.java`. On top of that, `InvoiceRetryCronJob.java` drives `InvoiceRetryService.java`, which reads `InvoiceRecordRepository.java`/`InvoiceStatus.java` and calls `InvoicingPort.java` to (re)push invoices that didn't succeed on the first attempt — a scheduled cron, not an immediate call. So a multi-day gap is consistent with either (a) the event listener processing lag/transactional-commit boundary, or (b) the invoice landing in a retry-needed `InvoiceStatus` and waiting for the next `InvoiceRetryCronJob` tick (interval is cron config, not in the graph — check `application-*.yml` in [3]) after an initial Fakturownia API failure.

The graph gives structure, not runtime timing/cron schedule or failure cause — open `InvoiceRetryCronJob.java`, `InvoiceCreatedEventListener.java`, and `InvoiceRetryService.java` to see the actual retry interval and failure-handling logic.
